To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

turbo coding can be used in DAB systems without modifying the puncture procedure, and that turbo coding can achieve the same performance as RCPC coding in the FIC and MSC for DAB transmission modes I on the Ricia fading channel and the Raligh fading channel.
the turbo coded OFDM system outperforms the RCPC coded OFDM system by 2.5 dB in the FIC for DAB transmission Mode I on the RICIAN fading channel.
the turbo code outperforms the existing RCPC codes in terms of bit-error rate (BER) and frame-error rate (FER) for DAB systems.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the turbo coding of the Eureka 145 DAB system.
a new turbo coded orthogonal frequency division modulation (OFDM) system that can be used for the DAB system.
a new system model and the comparison of the performance of this model with that of the conventional system model.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the new system is superior to the existing one in terms of the performance of the FIC and the performance of the MSC.
the new system model has better performance than the conventional one, especially in the FIC.

a new system model with turbo coded orthogonal frequency division (TCOFDM) has the potential to provide a higher bit error rate performance than the conventional DAB system model with RCPC coded orthogonal frequency division modulation (RCPCOFDM).
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the turbo coded OFDM system can provide a higher coding gain than the RCPC coded OFDM system, especially in a high signal to noise ratio (SNR) region.

, in the FIC, a turbo coded orthogonal frequency division multiple access (OFDMA) system can provide a 1.6 dB gain at a bit error rate of 1×10 ^{−2}, and, in the MSC, the system can provide a gain of 1 dB at a bit error of 1× 10 ^{−2.}
the proposed system model is superior to the existing one for both the FIC and the MSC in terms of BER performance and bandwidth efficiency.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the turbo coded DAB system has a better performance than the conventional RCPC coded DAB system.
the turbo code is superior to the existing RCPC coding in terms of the required signal-to-noise ratio (SNR) to maintain the bit error rate (BER) below 10(-3).
the turbo coded orthogonal frequency division modulation (OFDM) system is superior to the existing RCPC coded OFDM system in terms of the bit error rate (BER) performance and the system throughput.
